finding.title: Merge duplicate Completion/CompletionEvent DataClass groups in user_database_managers_test.dart
finding.why: 'Completion DataClass + managers' (line 431-489) and 'CompletionEvent DataClass + managers' (line 493-549) both insert a CompletionEventsCompanion, fetch it back via db.managers.completionEvents, and assert toJson/fromJson/copyWith/equality/hashCode/toString/toCompanion/copyWithCompanion on the exact same generated class — under two names, one of which ("Completion") is the pre-rename table name that test/helpers/drift_memory.dart documents as dropped ("NOTE (W3.20): The `completions` legacy table was dropped"). ~60 lines of redundant assertions run on every CI pass for zero incremental coverage, and a reader cannot tell whether the split is deliberate (e.g. with/without trackId) or a leftover from the rename.
finding.recommendation: Delete one group (or merge into one using current completionEvents/CompletionEvent terminology); if both variants are intentionally kept to cover trackId-present vs trackId-absent, add a one-line comment saying so.
acceptance_criteria: Only one group asserts the CompletionEvent DataClass round-trip, or a comment explains why two remain.

finding.title: Remove dead ProfileDao import in user_database_managers_test.dart:12
finding.why: `ProfileDao` (a DatabaseAccessor class, not an extension) is never referenced anywhere in the 1073-line file. `unused_import` is absent from analysis_options.yaml's hand-rolled lint list (confirmed by grep), so `flutter analyze` — clean in the audit baseline — does not and will not catch this or future dead imports in this file.
finding.recommendation: Delete the import. Separately, consider adding `unused_import` to the explicit lint list so this class of defect gets a Rule-0 checker.
acceptance_criteria: Line 12 import removed; dart analyze stays clean.
(Optional, stated separately) unused_import enabled in analysis_options.yaml so `flutter analyze`/`make audit` flags dead imports automatically going forward.

finding.title: Wire tool/schema_check.dart into CI and extend its whitelist to Goals/PriorCompletionImports/PointsLedger/RewardRedemptions
finding.rule: profileId-in-PK Invariant / Rule 0 (a checker only counts if it runs)

evidence.quote: Completions, Goals, LearningLedger, Streaks: profile-scoped but lack a composite UNIQUE/index today.
No user-facing Drift table may use a single-column autoincrement primary key without also specifying `profileId`
class Goals extends Table { IntColumn get id => integer().autoIncrement()();

finding.why: Ran `dart run tool/schema_check.dart` (passes, 13 tables) and re-ran it with an expanded --whitelist covering the rest of this batch: it FAILS on Goals, PointsLedger, RewardRedemptions and PriorCompletionImports — all real profile-scoped mutable tables with zero composite-key protection, sitting outside `_defaultWhitelist` since Story 25.6. The tool's own comment (line 44-46) says LearningLedger/StreakEvents are 'omitted' for lacking protection, but both are actually in the whitelist — the comment is stale. Separately, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` never invokes `schema-check`/`schema_check.dart` (only conditional `make audit`, analyze, and format run); the ROOT Makefile's `ci` target does include `schema-check` but nothing in CI calls root `make ci`, so the checker only ever runs if a developer remembers to type it manually. And docs/coding-standards.md describes a stricter, different rule ("single-column autoincrement... forbidden", enforcement = "make audit") than what the real tool implements (3 accepted shapes, run via `make schema-check`) — a contributor reading only the docs would misjudge which of their tables pass. This exact gap is how PointsLedger/RewardRedemptions (see companion P1 finding) shipped unprotected.
finding.recommendation: Add a CI step running `dart run tool/schema_check.dart` (or `make schema-check`) on every PR. Add 'PriorCompletionImports', 'PointsLedger', 'RewardRedemptions' to `_defaultWhitelist` after giving them a composite index (see companion findings); document Goals as a deliberate exemption (docstring already states multiple goals per curriculum are intentional, so no natural key applies) rather than silently omitting it. Refresh the stale comment and correct docs/coding-standards.md's profileId-in-PK section to name the real tool/command and the real 3-shape rule.
acceptance_criteria: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs schema_check.dart (or make schema-check) and fails the build on non-zero exit.
`dart run tool/schema_check.dart --whitelist <all mutable profile-scoped tables>` exits 0.
docs/coding-standards.md's profileId-in-PK section names tool/schema_check.dart / make schema-check and the three accepted shapes (primaryKey / uniqueKeys / @TableIndex).

finding.title: Rename outbox_table.dart and text_download_status.dart to match their table class names
finding.rule: File naming conventions (filename = snake_case of its class)
finding.why: Every other file in this 27-file directory names itself as the exact snake_case of its table class (bookmarks.dart↔Bookmarks, curriculum_tracks.dart↔CurriculumTracks, ...). outbox_table.dart carries a redundant `_table` suffix no sibling has (class is just `Outbox`); text_download_status.dart is singular while its class `TextDownloadStatuses` is plural. Minor but real: `grep -l 'class TextDownloadStatus'` or guessing the file for `Outbox` from the class name fails.
finding.recommendation: Rename outbox_table.dart → outbox.dart and text_download_status.dart → text_download_statuses.dart; update imports.
acceptance_criteria: git grep for the old filenames returns nothing; flutter analyze / build_runner stay green after rename.

finding.title: Fix completion_events.dart docstring — natural key description omits curriculumId that the enforced index actually includes
finding.why: The docstring's stated natural key (4 columns) doesn't match the @TableIndex it sits directly above (5 columns, adds curriculumId). A maintainer trusting the prose when writing a new dedup check or merger elsewhere would build the wrong key.
finding.recommendation: Update the docstring to list all 5 columns (or drop curriculumId from the index if it was never intended — needs a one-line confirmation from whoever added it in DNI-323).
acceptance_criteria: Docstring and @TableIndex column list textually match.
